text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - This is called fan-out on read — a single read request fans out to create many more requests

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Fan-out-on-write means: when someone posts, write their postId into every follower's PrecomputedFeed row.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: That's fine for a normal user with 300 followers — 300 writes. But Justin Bieber has 90 million followers.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: One tweet = 90 million writes, all triggered by a single createPost call. That's the "hot write" problem — the mirror image of the hot read problem the Post cache solved.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: The key insight: don't treat every account the same

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: isPrecomputed: false gets set on all follow rows pointing at Bieber — every one of his 90M followers has a row saying "don't push posts from Bieber into my precomputed feed."

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Write side: the async worker simply skips these

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: When Bieber posts, this function does almost nothing — no queue backlog, no 90M writes, no cost. The problem is solved not by making the write faster,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: but by not doing the write at all for this account.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: If we never wrote Bieber's posts into anyone's precomputed feed, those posts have to come from somewhere when a follower opens their feed.
